course.title: Atomic – Cambridge Lower Secondary Mathematics — Stage 7

unit.title: Shapes, Area and Volume
unit.blurb: Converting area units, hectares, the area of a triangle, and the volume and surface area of cubes and cuboids.
unit.subject: maths

O1.t: Convert between area units: mm², cm² and m².

O2.t: Know that 1 hectare = 10 000 m² and convert between hectares and square metres.

O3.t: Use the formula area = ½ × base × height for triangles.

O4.t: Calculate the volume of cubes and cuboids.

O5.t: Calculate the surface area of cubes and cuboids from their nets.

p: To change to a smaller unit, multiply; to change to a bigger unit, divide.
1 m² is NOT 100 cm². It is 100 × 100 = 10 000 cm².

p: A triangle is **half** of a rectangle with the same base and height: **Area = ½ × base × height**.
The height is **perpendicular** (at 90°) to the base.
base × height gives the rectangle; divide by 2 for the triangle.

sections.title: Calculating the volume of cubes and cuboids

p: **Volume** is the space inside a 3D shape, measured in cubic units such as cm³.
**Volume of a cuboid = length × width × height.** A cube with edge a has volume a³.
Volume is in cm³ (cubic), not cm².

rubric.pt: length × width gives the number of cubes in one layer
multiply by the height for the number of layers

req.reason: Length × width tells you how many 1 cm cubes cover the bottom layer. The height tells you how many layers there are, so multiply by the height.

sections.title: Calculating the surface area of cubes and cuboids

p: The **surface area** is the total area of all the faces. A cuboid has 6 rectangular faces in 3 matching pairs.
**Surface area = 2(lw + lh + wh).** A cube with edge a has surface area 6a².
Remember the faces you cannot see in the picture.
